The '''European Working Group on Multiple Criteria Decision Aiding''' (also, '''EURO Working Group on Multicriteria Decision Aiding''', '''EWG on Multicriteria Aid for Decisions''', or '''EWG-MCDA''') is a [[working group]] whose objective is to promote original research in the field of [[Multi-criteria decision analysis|multicriteria decision aiding]] at the European level.<ref name="http://www.cs.put.poznan.pl/ewgmcda">http://www.cs.put.poznan.pl/ewgmcda - EWG-MCDA webpage</ref> 

EWG-MCDA is one of the working groups of EURO, the [[Association of European Operational Research Societies]], and has approximately 350 members from 38 countries. The Group was founded in 1975<ref>Ballestero, E. and Romero, C. (1998). ''Decision Making and its Applications to Economic Problems'', Kluwer Academic Publishers, Boston. p. 9. {{ISBN|0-7923-8238-2}}</ref> by [[Bernard Roy]] during the First European Conference on Operational Research (EURO I) held in Brussels, Belgium.<ref name="http://www.euro-online.org">http://www.euro-online.org - EURO, Association of European Operational Research Societies</ref>

The objectives of the EURO Working Group on MCDA are the following:<ref name="http://www.cs.put.poznan.pl/ewgmcda"/><ref name="http://www.euro-online.org"/>
* to contribute to the development, at a European level, of an original way of thinking in the field of multicriteria decision aiding;
* to allow each member of the group to present to others methodological, theoretical or applied results, to submit his/her own work and thoughts to critical discussion by the group, and also to facilitate collaboration;
* to develop multicriteria aid for decisions by facilitating contact between all people interested in the subject, and by stimulating continuity and progress in exchanges and work;
* to keep the group alive and open by means of bi-annual meetings which should not be mini-conferences but real meetings favourable to exchanges and to the emergence of new ideas.

Since 1975, the Working Group has met invariably twice a year. The 50th Anniversary meeting of the Group was held in 1999 at the château of the [[Centre culturel international de Cerisy-la-Salle|Centre Culturel International de Cerisy-la-Salle]], in France. At the 72nd Meeting of the Group held in 2010 at the Ecole Centrale Paris, Bernard Roy stepped down from his position of the Group Coordinator and became the Honorary Chairman.<ref name="Newsletter/Fall10">http://www.cs.put.poznan.pl/ewgmcda/newsletter/Fall10.pdf -  EWG-MCDA Newsletter, Series 3, Number 22, Fall 2010</ref>

==The European School of MCDA==

Most of the researchers or authors distinguish two major streams of MCDA methods:<ref name="Zopounidis01">C. Zopounidis (2001). Financial applications of multicriteria analysis. In C. Floudas and P. Pardalos, editors, ''Encyclopedia of Optimization'', volume II, pages 114-125. Springer, Dordrecht, The Netherlands. {{ISBN|0-7923-7027-9}}</ref> 
* the American School or School of the MultiAttribute Utility Theory (MAUT), and
* the European school or methods of outranking and synthesis.

The development of the European School of Multiple Criteria Decision Aiding is mainly attributed to the EURO Working Group on MCDA.<ref name="Roy96">B. Roy and D. Vanderpooten (1996). An overview on "The European School of MCDA: Emergence, Basic Features and Current Works". ''Journal of Multi-Criteria Decision Analysis'', 5(1):22-37. ISSN 0377-2217, {{doi|10.1016/S0377-2217(96)00379-7}}</ref><ref name="Doumpos02">M. Doumpos and C. Zopounidis (2002). ''Multicriteria Decision Aid Classification Methods'', volume 73 of Applied Optimization. Springer, Dordrecht, The Netherlands. {{ISBN|1-4020-0805-8}}</ref> The European School directs its study to methodologies where the personal preferences of decision makers have less influence on the alternative chosen.

The methods of the European School are the ELECTRE family methods (ELimination Et Choix Traduisant la REalité) which stems from the pioneering work of Bernard Roy and whose development is strongly connected with the birth of the EWG on MCDA,<ref name="Figueira05">J. Figueira, V. Mousseau and B. Roy (2005). ELECTRE Methods, In ''Multiple Criteria Decision Analysis: State of the Art Surveys'', J. Figueira, S. Greco, M. Ehrgott (Editors), Int. Series in Operations Research and Management Science, Vol. 78, 133-172, Springer, New York. {{ISBN|0-387-23067-X}}</ref> and the PROMETHEE (PReference ranking Organization METHod for Enrichment Evaluations) method initiated by Professor Jean-Pierre Brans in the beginning of the eighties.
